title: Persian GPT — 110M Transformer From Scratch
description: A 110.4M-parameter decoder-only transformer trained end to end for Persian. The project covers a cleaned Wikipedia corpus, custom 32K BPE tokenizer, training pipeline, n-gram baselines, and held-out evaluation.
type: Flagship model · Persian NLP · From-scratch training
note: A research portfolio model; the held-out perplexity is a language-model metric, not an instruction-following benchmark.

research.context: This project demonstrates an end-to-end low-resource language-model workflow for Persian, from corpus preparation through tokenizer design, training, and held-out evaluation.
research.limitations: The reported perplexity is specific to the held-out corpus and tokenizer. It is not a measure of factuality, instruction following, or downstream task performance.

caseStudy.title: Persian GPT from scratch: a 110M parameter language model
caseStudy.description: A 110.4M-parameter Persian GPT trained from scratch on cleaned Wikipedia text with a 32K BPE tokenizer, PyTorch, and held-out perplexity evaluation.
caseStudy.lede: An end-to-end Persian language-modeling experiment, from preparing a cleaned Wikipedia corpus and building a tokenizer to training a decoder-only Transformer and comparing held-out perplexity against n-gram baselines.
caseStudy.challenge: Persian has fewer openly documented from-scratch training examples than high-resource languages. The goal here was to build a transparent, reproducible baseline workflow and document what the resulting language-model metric does and does not establish.
approach: Cleaned and prepared 855,724 Persian Wikipedia documents, totaling about 244 million training tokens.
Trained a custom 32,000-token byte-pair encoding tokenizer on the prepared corpus.
Implemented and trained a 110.4M-parameter decoder-only Transformer in PyTorch for two epochs (7,450 training steps).
Evaluated the held-out split with loss and perplexity, then compared perplexity with unigram and interpolated 5-gram baselines.
results: The held-out interpolated 5-gram baseline perplexity was 171.60, and the unigram baseline was 1,590.26.
The reported language-model metrics apply only to the documented corpus split and tokenizer.
caseStudy.limitations: This is a small research portfolio model trained on Wikipedia text. It is not an instruction-following or factual question-answering system, has no retrieval grounding, and has not been evaluated for broad Persian fluency, safety, or downstream usefulness. Perplexity does not establish factuality or real-world performance.

title: 3D Cardiac MRI Segmentation
description: A complete 3D cardiac MRI segmentation pipeline using PyTorch, MONAI, and a 3D U-Net. It covers NIfTI loading, preprocessing, mixed-precision training, sliding-window inference, and voxel-level evaluation on Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task02 Heart.
note: Research project on a public benchmark dataset; not clinically validated or deployed for clinical decision-making.

research.context: The project investigates voxel-level cardiac structure segmentation from volumetric MRI, a setting where models must use three-dimensional spatial context.
research.limitations: The reported validation Dice is from this project’s benchmark split. The system has not been clinically validated and is not a clinical decision-support tool.

caseStudy.title: 3D cardiac MRI segmentation with MONAI and a 3D U-Net
caseStudy.description: A cardiac MRI segmentation pipeline built with PyTorch, MONAI, the Task02 Heart benchmark, a 3D U-Net, and sliding-window inference.
caseStudy.lede: This project segments cardiac structures in volumetric MRI. It documents a complete research pipeline from NIfTI loading and preprocessing through mixed-precision training, sliding-window inference, and validation-set Dice evaluation.
caseStudy.challenge: Cardiac MRI volumes contain three-dimensional spatial context, so the workflow needs to preserve volumetric information through preprocessing, training, and inference. The project focuses on a public benchmark task and transparent reporting of its validation result.
approach: Used the Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task02 Heart dataset and NIfTI volumes.
Built preprocessing and data-loading steps with PyTorch and MONAI.
Trained a 3D U-Net with DiceCELoss and AdamW for 100 epochs, using mixed precision (FP16).
Applied sliding-window inference to full 3D volumes and evaluated voxel-level overlap with Dice.
results: Best reported validation Dice: 0.8821 on the documented benchmark split.
Training configuration: 100 epochs, 3D U-Net, mixed-precision training.
The result is a project-reported benchmark validation metric, not a clinical performance estimate.
caseStudy.limitations: This work has not been clinically validated, prospectively tested, or evaluated across external institutions and scanner settings. It is not a diagnostic device or clinical decision-support system. The validation score describes only the project’s benchmark split.

title: AI Research Assistant Platform
description: A multi-agent research assistant built with LangGraph, ChromaDB RAG, FastAPI, and LangSmith. Planning, retrieval, parallel research, tool execution, citation-grounded synthesis, bounded reflection, persistent state, and streaming are covered in the public implementation.
note: Offline tests use a deterministic fake-LLM mode; the test count measures exercised software behavior, not answer quality.

research.context: This system explores how retrieval, web research, tools, synthesis, and bounded reflection can be orchestrated and tested as a stateful research workflow.
methods: LangGraph stateful workflow with parallel branches
ChromaDB retrieval and local ONNX embeddings
SQLite persistence and FastAPI REST/SSE endpoints
Deterministic offline suite plus LangSmith evaluation tooling
research.limitations: The offline suite validates application contracts with deterministic model behavior. It does not establish comparative research-answer quality or clinical safety.

caseStudy.title: Multi-agent AI research assistant with LangGraph and RAG
caseStudy.description: A multi-agent research assistant using LangGraph, ChromaDB RAG, FastAPI, parallel research, cited synthesis, persistent state, and offline tests.
caseStudy.lede: A full-stack research workflow that combines planning, retrieval, parallel research, tool execution, cited synthesis, bounded reflection, persistent state, and server-sent event streaming.
caseStudy.challenge: Research tasks often require several different operations: break down a query, retrieve relevant material, gather evidence, synthesize findings, and preserve progress. This project explores how to orchestrate those steps in a testable, stateful application.
approach: Used LangGraph to coordinate five roles and parallel research branches.
Connected ChromaDB retrieval with local ONNX embeddings and configurable research tools.
Implemented FastAPI REST and server-sent event (SSE) interfaces, with SQLite checkpointing for persistent workflow state.
Added citation-grounded synthesis, bounded reflection, LangSmith evaluation tooling, and deterministic offline tests.
results: The repository reports 103 offline tests for application behavior in deterministic fake-LLM mode.
The workflow exposes REST and SSE interfaces and includes five agent roles.
Tests exercise software contracts; they are not a measure of answer correctness, evidence quality, or research usefulness.
caseStudy.limitations: The deterministic fake-LLM test mode validates application behavior rather than live-model answer quality. The system has not been shown to outperform human research workflows or establish the correctness and completeness of generated research. Human verification of cited sources remains necessary.

title: CohortSeal
description: Patient-level split audits catch patient and exact-duplicate leakage before model evaluation. CohortSeal creates reproducible group splits and stores findings in SQLite, with CLI and FastAPI workflows plus MONAI, DICOM, and Hugging Face adapters.

title: Holdout Ledger: Dataset Leakage Audit Workbench
description: A local workbench for inspecting text and entity overlap across train, validation, and test splits. Includes an evidence dashboard, offline reports, SQLite audit snapshots, and reviewed repair plans that preserve every test record. CI checks track newly exposed holdout IDs; lexical detection limits are documented.

title: Agent Guardrails — Five Composable Skills for AI Coding Agents
description: A lifecycle of five Agent Skills that gate AI coding agents before expensive mistakes happen. recon researches the task and proposes self-rules; preflight runs the cheapest version first and estimates cost as a range; hold stops on unhandled failures and offers three recovery options; scope catches drift outside agreed boundaries; budget enforces the preflight estimate. Portable across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Copilot via the open Agent Skills standard.
